name: Adamson et al. 2016 Perturb-seq, K562 CRISPRi single perturbations: unseen-perturbation expression prediction (Csendes et al. 2025 Supplementary Table 2)
description: Pseudo-bulk Pearson correlations between predicted and observed post-perturbation expression for unseen perturbations, in raw and control-subtracted space.

attributes.protocol: Single-cell predictions are averaged per perturbation and compared with the observed pseudo-bulk profile. Pearson: raw expression. Pearson Delta: perturbed minus control expression. DE variants use the top 20 differentially expressed genes from the GEARS publication (t-test), the top 20 by Wilcoxon test, or the top 20 with the CRISPR target gene(s) removed.
attributes.source_locator: Results 'Benchmarking of post-perturbation RNA-seq prediction methods' paragraph 3; Methods 'Model evaluation'
limitations: One split per dataset; no seeds or spread printed.
Raw-expression Pearson is near 1 for every model and the authors do not consider it meaningful (Results paragraph 5).
Low perturbation-specific variance in these datasets limits how well they separate models (Results 'Limited perturbation diversity biases benchmarking outcomes').

name: Relevance of unseen-perturbation expression prediction on Adamson (K562 CRISPRi) (Csendes et al. 2025) to "Assess models for genetic perturbation experiments"
description: Two foundation models and thirteen simple controls (a Train Mean predictor and random forest, elastic net and kNN regressors on four perturbed-gene feature sets) are scored on the same unseen perturbations, which is the methods-and-controls comparison the use case asks for. It is proxy evidence: expression-prediction scores do not establish mechanism or experimental prioritisation (use-case exclusion), and the comparison is the authors' own baselines against reproduced foundation models.

attributes.endpoint: Pearson correlation of predicted versus observed expression change (Pearson Delta), plus raw-expression and top-20-DE variants, for scGPT, scFoundation, Train Mean and 12 feature-based regressors on unseen perturbations, Adamson (K562 CRISPRi)
attributes.rationale: Two foundation models and thirteen simple controls (a Train Mean predictor and random forest, elastic net and kNN regressors on four perturbed-gene feature sets) are scored on the same unseen perturbations, which is the methods-and-controls comparison the use case asks for. It is proxy evidence: expression-prediction scores do not establish mechanism or experimental prioritisation (use-case exclusion), and the comparison is the authors' own baselines against reproduced foundation models.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; splits, gene subsets and metric implementations differ between sources.
Use Pearson Delta rather than raw Pearson to compare models; raw Pearson is near 1 for all of them.
limitations: Datasets have low perturbation-specific variance (Results, second section), so differences between models are small.
Top-20 DE metrics include the CRISPR target gene unless stated, which favours scGPT (claim).

All authors are full-time employees of Turbine Ltd., and one is a founder (Competing interests). They built the Train Mean and regressor baselines, configured and ran the scGPT and scFoundation fine-tuning themselves, and argue that the baselines win; the foundation models were not run by their developers, so their configuration may not be the best available.

One GEARS perturbation-exclusive split per dataset, within one cell line, with one fine-tuning run per foundation model (best epoch on validation); no seeds, repeats or spread are printed, so small differences between models are not testable.
The Wilcoxon top-20 DE metric is blank for scGPT and scFoundation in Supplementary Table 2.
Results paragraphs 7 and 8 cite Supplementary Table 1 for values that are in Supplementary Table 2.
All perturbations are single-gene CRISPRi in one cell line, so the use case's combination-training and cross-cell-type exclusions are not engaged.

79 of the 116 test perturbations are two-gene combinations (9 with neither gene seen in training, 52 with one, 18 with both) and 37 are unseen single genes (Supplementary Table 1); every value pools them. The per-subgroup values (Supplementary Table 3) are not extracted because their metric is not labelled.

The make-up of the 138 training perturbations is not printed, so whether training included combination examples, which the use case requires for GEARS combination prediction, cannot be confirmed from this source. scFoundation runs through GEARS, so the use case's GEARS combination exclusion applies to it directly.
The regressors represent a combination as the sum of the two genes' embeddings (Methods 'Baseline models').
